## Problem

A Triton Inference Server speaks the KServe v2 protocol on three
default ports — HTTP 8000, gRPC 8001, metrics 8002 — and the control
surface rides the SAME HTTP port as inference: with the right shaped
POST, an unauthenticated client can ask the server to load or unload
models from a declared model-repository path at
`POST /v2/repository/models/<model>/load|unload` alongside
`POST /v2/repository/index`. Anyone who can reach the port can
inspect what is served (health + model index), drive inference, and —
the LLM10 half — change what is served. The quickstart posture makes
it worse for lab realism: upstream's own quickstart binds
`0.0.0.0:8000`. The manifest maps the surface to OWASP LLM02 + LLM10; the pre-purge
The paired attack row mapped to ATLAS AML.T0049 + T0050 (the row was a
phantom — removed, os#210; the protocol facts here stand on upstream
TRITON docs, not the removed row). You want to
demonstrate the exposure against the lab-booted server (the Shape-3
container posture: `triton-inference-server` ships as a
docker-wrapper row, podman, `autoStart=false`; A-7 never rides this
shape — the attack side drives the shapes from the base system at a
booted target), then flip the posture closed and see the probe
results invert.

## Solution

Two legs, one sweep, shape-for-shape:

```bash
# 1. BOOT THE LAB TARGET — triton is a docker-wrapper row (Shape 3):
#      kailash info triton-inference-server
#    -> packaging docker-wrapper (podman), autoStart=false, pin
#       semitechnologies/weaviate:1.39.2-style Shape-3 row (image
#       per upstream's quickstart container). Lab boot = turning the
#       backend on; the A-7 attack tooling NEVER rides inside that
#       container — probes run from the base system at the port.
#    Minimal lab posture for the exposed leg (isolated lab segment:
#      docker run --rm --gpus all --shm-size=256m -p 8000:8000 \
#        -v /models:/models tritonserver --model-repository=/models
#    (upstream's quickstart banner reads: Started HTTPService at
#     0.0.0.0:8000  — the broad bind is the thing being tested)

# 2. HEALTH + ENUMERATION (HTTP 8000, no credentials):
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/v2/health/live
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/v2/health/ready
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/v2/models/<model>/versions/<v>/ready
#    -> 200s; the KServe v2 readiness shapes

# 3. INFERENCE (the LLM02 half — protocol shape, no key checked):
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/v2/models/<model>/infer \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d {"inputs":[...],"outputs":[...]}
#    -> inference result per the model's declared I/O shape

# 4. MODEL-REPOSITORY CONTROL (the LLM10 half — the control surface):
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/v2/repository/index \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
#    -> [{"name":"<model>","version":"<v>","state":"READY"}, ...]
curl -fsS -X POST http://<target>:8000/v2/repository/models/<model>/load \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"parameters":{}}'
#    -> the server loads the model from the declared repo path
curl -fsS -X POST http://<target>:8000/v2/repository/models/<model>/unload \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
#    -> the server unloads it — inference now FAILS via #3; you just
#       toggled what the server serves, unauthenticated

# 5. METRICS (port 8002 — separate port, same reachability logic):
curl -fsS http://<target>:8002/metrics
#    -> Prometheus exposition (inference counts, latencies, cache)
```

Then the verification leg — flip the posture, re-run the same sweep:

```bash
# 6. THE FLIP (three controls, one deliberate posture):
#      a. bind: the server MUST NOT answer 0.0.0.0 in production —
#         the quickstart banner is a lab convenience, not a bind
#         recommendation; keep the container loopback-reachable only
#         (publish -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000, or put the container on an
#          isolated lab segment), and
#      b. metrics off at the server flag:
docker run --rm --gpus all --shm-size=256m -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /models:/models tritonserver --model-repository=/models \
     --allow-metrics=false
#      (the /metrics endpoint on 8002 is then absent — the exposition
#       stops being a segment-readable telemetry feed)
#      c. restricted-API gate (BETA surface): upstream exposes a
#         restriction mechanism that requires a key on the sensitive
#         APIs —
#         --http-restricted-api=<apis>:<restricted-key>=<restricted-value>
#         e.g. --http-restricted-api=repository-control:<key>=<val>
#         (BETA: a lab-grade gate, not a hardened perimeter)
nixos-rebuild test 2>/dev/null || docker stop <container>
#    (flip = stop the broad-bind container; re-boot with the posture
#     above, or the loopback-publish variant)

# 7. SAME sweep, same box:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://<target>:8000/v2/health/live
#    -> FAIL (refused) from the segment — loopback-publish closed the
#       whole port to the segment. /metrics absent (--allow-metrics
#       false); load/unload demand the restricted key. Diff = evidence.
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
sweep @ http://<target>:8000  posture: quickstart bind (0.0.0.0), no gate
  /v2/health/live      -> ok 200
  /v2/health/ready     -> ok 200
  /v2/models/<m>/infer -> ok (shape per model I/O)
  /v2/repository/index -> ok [{"name":"<m>","state":"READY"}]
  /v2/repository/models/<m>/load|unload -> ok (state toggled)
  :8002/metrics        -> ok exposition
sweep again, hardened posture (loopback-publish + flags)
  health/infer/index/load/unload -> FAIL (refused from segment)
  :8002/metrics        -> absent (flag off)
  repository control   -> key demanded where the restricted-API gate
                          covers it (BETA surface)
```

## Discussion

- **Why plain curl and not a bespoke exploit script:** the
  the paired attack manifest row was a PHANTOM — its claimed kailash-os
  upstream was never created — and the os#210 audit (2026-10-14)
  removed it entirely
  ([kailash-os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210);
  the name rides the registry there). The probe leg runs the verified
  KServe v2 shapes against the booted target with the base system
  only — nothing invented. A real A-7 tool re-enters later via the
  os#210 rebuild contract and installs through the double-key lab
  gate (walk: [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)).
- **Shape 3 is why the lab leg looks the way it does:** the
  triton-inference-server row is a docker-wrapper row — podman,
  `autoStart=false`, a pinned upstream container. In this book's
  packaging grammar, that is the Shape-3 posture (the packaging shape
  documented in docs/guide/o-03-docker-wrapper-stores.md), and the
  A-7 attack tooling NEVER rides inside that shape ("A-7 never in
  this shape" is the packaging note's line verbatim) — the A-7 attack
  rides a lab-booted container target while native attack tooling
  stays out of the container. The boot IS the lab posture: turning
  the backend on is what makes the target answer.
- **The load/unload verbs are the pair's teeth:** enumeration shows
  what is served; inference shows what it returns; the repository
  control pair changes what is served — unload the model and the
  same inference shape fails, load it back and it answers again.
  That toggle is the LLM10 evidence: control surface on the same
  unauthenticated port as the data surface.
- **The BETA gate is honest about being BETA:** `--http-restricted-api`
  (with its restricted key/value) is upstream's Beta restricted-API
  mechanism — better than nothing, worth using, but a Beta surface is
  not a hardened perimeter; the bind + firewall remain the
  load-bearing controls, and vLLM's identical story (key never covered
  everything) is a different server with the same moral: perimeter
  beats flag.
- **The observability defence leg is a pending row, stated honestly:**
  Phoenix (Arize) is the trace destination: OTLP/HTTP exporter to
  `:6006/v1/traces` (gRPC :4317), server via `phoenix serve`; and
  Evidently is the report layer — `Report`/`DataDefinition` +
  column descriptors over captured request logs, producing the drift/
  data-quality view that makes an unexplained inference spike visible.
  Both are d-02 rows with upstream config flows that exist; their
  kailash module wiring is PENDING at the pin — quoted as the design,
  not as a landed surface. The traces/reports become the standing
  anomaly view that the probes hand-verified during the pair.
- **This is the transferable pattern:** lab target up → probe sweep
  → posture flip → same sweep → diff. Origin walk with the verdict
  instrument: [Attack the platform, then
  verify](attack-then-verify.html).
